title: Child Abuse and Neglect
summary: What child abuse is, how common severe violence against children is, its psychological and sexual forms, its effects on development, and how abusive families can be helped.

lesson.title: When carers become the danger
lesson.hook: We often picture danger to children as strangers. Yet the person most likely to seriously hurt a child is usually someone inside the home, the very person meant to protect them.

slides.heading: Defining child abuse
slides.body:
**Child abuse** happens when an adult **deliberately** (not by accident) uses **excessive force, physical or psychological**, against a child, often meaning to **harm or crush** the child.

A wider definition covers any **physical, sexual or psychological mistreatment**, or **neglect**, of children, particularly by **parents or other carers**. It has an **enormous impact** on psychological development.

slides.heading: A survivor's memory
slides.story: A woman interviewed by TIME magazine in 1983 recalled a childhood of constant beatings by her mother, with shoes, belts and kitchen tools. When she threatened to tell the police, her mother frightened her into silence. After each beating came hugs and apologies. As a child she would sit outside and quietly dream of finding a different mother.
slides.takeaway: Abuse often mixes violence with affection and threats, trapping the child in fear and confusion.

slides.heading: How common is it?
slides.body:
Surveys in the United States suggest about **1 in every 10 children** suffers **severe violence**: **kicking**, **biting**, **hitting**, **beating**, or threats with **weapons such as knives or guns**.

Some observers believe **physical abuse and neglect** are among the **leading causes of death** in young children.

slides.question: Which of the following counts as severe violence against a child?
slides.why: Kicking, biting, beating and threats with weapons are forms of severe violence.

slides.heading: Who is abused, and by whom
slides.body:
**Boys and girls** are physically abused at about the **same rate**. Abuse happens in **all socio-economic groups**, though it is **more common among the poor**, where stresses pile up.

Abusers are **usually the parents**, which makes abuse hard to detect and hard for children to escape or report.

slides.heading: Neglect
slides.body:
**Neglect** is the failure to meet a child's basic needs: **food, shelter, clothing, hygiene, medical care, supervision, education** and **emotional care**. It is often less visible than beatings but can be just as damaging, and sometimes fatal.

As earlier units showed, severe early neglect can also lead to **reactive attachment disorder**.

slides.heading: Effects on development
slides.body:
Abused children are at higher risk of **anxiety, depression, post-traumatic stress, low self-esteem, aggression**, school difficulties and later **substance abuse**.

Abuse can also pass across generations: a minority of abused children, often estimated at around **a third**, go on to abuse their own children. Most do **not**, especially when they receive support.

slides.question: Child abuse is:
options: Found in all socio-economic groups, though more common among the poor
slides.why: Abuse crosses all classes, but poverty-related stress makes it more common among poorer families.

slides.heading: How your lecturer will ask this
slides.body: Expect 'define child abuse' and 'list the various forms of severe violence against children'. Use the definition with 'non-accidental' and 'excessive physical or psychological force'. Know that boys and girls are abused at similar rates and that parents are usually the abusers. Trap: claiming abuse only happens in poor homes.
slides.sampleQuestion: List five forms of severe violence against children.
slides.howToAnswer: Being kicked, bitten, hit, beaten, and threatened with a knife or gun. Add that about 1 in 10 children experiences such violence in US surveys.

points: Child abuse: non-accidental, excessive physical or psychological force by an adult.
About 1 in 10 children suffers severe violence in US surveys.
Boys and girls are abused equally; abusers are usually parents.
Abuse occurs in all classes, more among the poor.
Neglect and abuse harm emotional, social and academic development.

questions.explanation: I and III are correct. Abuse occurs across all socio-economic groups.

options: Poor parents love their children less
Stresses such as unemployment and crowding can trigger abusive behaviour

sections.name: Psychological and sexual abuse, and help

lesson.title: Invisible wounds and healing
lesson.hook: Bruises fade in weeks. Being called 'useless' every day for ten years can shape how a person sees themselves for life. Which leaves the deeper mark?

slides.heading: Psychological abuse
slides.body:
**Psychological abuse** includes **severe or excessive discipline**, **scapegoating** (blaming one child for everything), **ridicule**, **isolation**, and **refusing help** to a child with psychological problems.

It probably **accompanies all** physical abuse and neglect, and it also often occurs **on its own**, leaving no visible marks.

slides.heading: The family scapegoat
slides.story: In one household, everything that goes wrong is blamed on 11-year-old Uche: the broken plate, the father's lost job, even the rain. He is mocked in front of visitors and kept away from his cousins' parties. No one has ever hit him, yet he believes he is cursed and worthless.
slides.takeaway: Psychological abuse, through scapegoating, ridicule and isolation, harms a child deeply without leaving a single bruise.

slides.question: Repeatedly blaming one child for all the family's problems is an example of:
options: Scapegoating, a form of psychological abuse
slides.why: Scapegoating is a form of psychological abuse.

slides.heading: Child sexual abuse
slides.body:
**Child sexual abuse** is the **use of a child to satisfy adult sexual desires**. It can happen **inside or outside** the home and appears **equally common across all social classes, races and ethnic groups**.

Surveys indicate that **13% or more of women** were made to have sexual contact with a grown man while they were children, often a **father or stepfather**, and **at least 4% of men** were sexually abused as children.

right.title: Sexual abuse
points: Equal across all classes and groups
At least 13% of women, 4% of men
Often by fathers, stepfathers or known adults

slides.heading: Treating abusive families
slides.body:
Treatment often focuses on **parents**. Therapies help them gain **insight** into their behaviour, offer **training in alternatives** to abuse, and teach **parenting skills**.

Other approaches help parents cope with the **stresses** that often **trigger** abuse: **unemployment, marital conflict** and **depression**. The child also needs therapy, safety, and sometimes a protected placement.

slides.heading: Protecting children in Nigeria
slides.body:
Nigeria's **Child Rights Act (2003)** sets out children's rights to protection from abuse, neglect and exploitation; states adopt it into their own laws. The **VAPP Act (2015)** also criminalises many forms of violence.

Teachers, health workers and neighbours often notice abuse first. Knowing the **signs**, unexplained injuries, fearfulness, sudden withdrawal, sexual knowledge beyond the child's age, helps children get help sooner.

slides.question: Which treatment approach helps parents handle the stresses that often trigger abuse?
options: Helping with unemployment, marital conflict and depression
slides.why: Reducing triggering stresses lowers the risk of further abuse.

slides.heading: How your lecturer will ask this
slides.body: Expect 'list and explain two forms of child abuse': psychological and sexual. Define each and give features and figures (13% of women, 4% of men). Objectives contrast class patterns: physical abuse more common among the poor, sexual abuse equal across classes. Also know treatment: insight, alternatives, parenting skills, stress management.
slides.sampleQuestion: List and explain two forms of child abuse.
slides.howToAnswer: Psychological abuse: excessive discipline, scapegoating, ridicule, isolation, refusing help; often with physical abuse. Sexual abuse: using a child for adult sexual gratification, inside or outside the home, equal across classes.

points: Psychological abuse: excessive discipline, scapegoating, ridicule, isolation.
It accompanies physical abuse and also occurs alone.
Sexual abuse: using a child for adult gratification; equal across classes.
At least 13% of women and 4% of men report childhood sexual abuse.
Treatment: parent insight, alternatives, skills, stress management; protect the child.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a form of psychological abuse?
questions.explanation: Ridicule and isolation are psychological abuse.

questions.explanation: At least 13% of women report such experiences.

options: Equally common across classes, races and ethnic groups
questions.explanation: Unlike physical abuse, it is spread evenly across groups.

questions.stem: Psychological abuse probably:
options: Accompanies all physical abuse and neglect, and also occurs alone
questions.explanation: It goes with all forms of maltreatment and also occurs by itself.

questions.stem: Parents refuse to take their severely depressed daughter for help, saying 'she is just lazy'. This is an example of:
options: Psychological abuse through refusal of help
questions.explanation: Refusing help for a child's psychological problems is psychological abuse.

questions.stem: A therapist teaches a father who hits his children other ways to discipline and how to manage his anger. This approach provides:
questions.explanation: Insight plus training in alternatives to abuse is a core treatment.

questions.stem: A mother began beating her children after losing her job and falling into depression. Treatment should especially address:
questions.explanation: Stresses such as unemployment and depression often trigger abuse.

questions.stem: All of the following are forms of psychological abuse EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Age-appropriate chores are not abuse.

questions.stem: Which pair is correctly matched?
options: Physical abuse: equal across all classes
Sexual abuse: equal across all classes
questions.explanation: Sexual abuse is equally common across classes; physical abuse is more common among the poor.

questions.stem: At least what percentage of men were sexually abused in childhood, according to surveys cited?
questions.explanation: At least 4% of men report childhood sexual abuse.

questions.stem: I. Sexual abuse can occur inside or outside the home. II. Many female victims were abused by fathers or stepfathers. III. Treatment of abuse focuses only on punishing parents. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: I and II are correct. Treatment includes insight, skills and stress management, not only punishment.

questions.stem: Why is psychological abuse often harder to detect than physical abuse?
options: It usually leaves no visible marks
questions.explanation: Without bruises or injuries, it can go unnoticed.

questions.stem: Which combination best describes a complete response to a case of child abuse?
options: Ensure the child's safety, provide therapy for the child, and help parents with insight, skills and stress
Ignore it as a family matter
questions.explanation: Effective responses protect the child and address parents' behaviour and stresses.
